name: Kiribati
headline: Kiribati: +4.3% growth in 2025, 5.9% inflation, debt 8% of GDP
sections: Kiribati is a $349 million economy (2025), the world's 212th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +4.3% in 2025, faster than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $3,937 at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 4.2% of GDP (2024).
Consumer prices rose 5.9% in 2025, above typical targets.
Gross government debt is 8% of GDP (2025), a low level that has fallen from 21% in 2020. The general government balance is −14.5% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is −15.2% of GDP (2025), a sizeable external financing need. Trade equals 102% of GDP (2024), a highly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 1.2% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 36% of GDP by 2031, still rising from today's level. Life expectancy is 66.6 years (2024). Population: 129 thousand (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
